natural_body: Targeted 40% discounts boost acquisition but sharply damage retention.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the domain of memory_86 and memory_31, both of which report durable activation/completion lifts from simplifying onboarding for self-serve/SMB accounts. This is a more targeted fix for a measured internal metric decline than activation_messaging (which addresses week-one engagement broadly) and carries less downstream risk than promotional_pricing, which memory_73 explicitly flags as damaging retention despite acquisition gains — a serious concern given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not just short-term acquisition against competitor pricing pressure. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive are valuable but don't address the acute onboarding/activation declines this week. I want to verify memory_31 (foundational, older, and central to my chosen action) to confirm the original effect size and conditions still apply, and memory_73 to confirm the retention-damage finding is robust, since competitor pricing pressure will likely tempt a promotional_pricing move later and I want that risk well-substantiated rather than assumed. Given only one experiment slot and two plausible-but-overlapping onboarding memories, I'm scaling this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout to preserve optionality if effects don't replicate exactly as recorded.
